comparison: Both evaluations support the sensor development and characterization claims (C21-C25, C27-C29). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the optimization process with quantitative fluorescence responses. Peer review confirms 'the evidence for these tools working as advertised is solid' and accepts the technical characterization without dispute. Strong agreement on sensor functionality.

Both evaluations support claims about impaired signaling in GLPLight1 (C30-C34). OpenEval emphasizes the importance of demonstrating the sensor doesn't trigger endogenous signaling with quantified EC50 values. Peer review explicitly acknowledges the ~1000-fold sensitivity difference between native receptor and sensor. Agreement on this key characterization.

Both evaluations support ligand specificity claims (C35-C41). OpenEval details quantitative EC50 measurements and validation against literature SAR data. Peer review explicitly confirms 'its specificity is high, as shown by lack of response to ligands of related class B GPCRs.' Strong agreement on pharmacological validation.

Both evaluations support the alanine scanning validation (C42-C45). OpenEval emphasizes agreement with known SAR from literature. Peer review implicitly accepts this application without critique, suggesting acceptance of the sensor's utility for structure-activity studies. Agreement on validation approach.

Both evaluations address endogenous GLP-1 detection (C46-C47) but differ in confidence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveat about lacking direct GLP-1 measurement controls. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning 'whether binding alone is demonstrated versus functional detection' and wanting to see 'an actual fluorescence response to stimulated release.' Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Both evaluations support photo-GLP1 synthesis and functional validation (C48-C53, C7, C69). OpenEval emphasizes thorough chemical characterization and functional validation with GLPLight1. Peer review confirms 'the evidence for these tools working as advertised is solid' and accepts that photo-GLP1 has no detectable activity until light activation. Strong agreement on basic functionality.

Both evaluations address slowed activation kinetics of caged compound (C54-C55) but differ in assessment. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the mechanistic interpretation reasonable based on class B1 GPCR biology. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning 'whether the kinetics of the response to PhotoGLP1 itself would mimic the normal activation by GLP-1 in the absence of the caged compound.' Disagreement on interpretation validity.

Both evaluations support spatial control demonstrations (C56-C57, C71, C8). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls and that spatial resolution is limited by optical uncaging rather than diffusion. Peer review implicitly accepts this as part of 'working as advertised' without specific challenge. Agreement on spatial precision capability.

Both evaluations address single-cell cAMP signaling (C58-C59) but differ in confidence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the critical negative control and single-cell specificity. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, concerned that 'light-dependence was evaluated only with the GLPLight1 sensor and not with GLP1R signaling itself, which is 1000x more sensitive.' Disagreement on validation sufficiency.

Both evaluations support the mechanistic interpretation of sensor kinetics (C60-C62). OpenEval finds the linking of slower kinetics to class B1 binding mechanism reasonable and well-supported by citations. Peer review accepts this interpretation without challenge as an accepted insight from sensor characterization. Agreement on mechanistic understanding.

Both evaluations address EC50 discrepancy and physiological implications (C63-C64, C66-C67, C65). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the discrepancy may be confounded by assay differences and that C65 is speculative. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning practical applicability: 'difficult to see how the sensor will be useful for in vivo detection of GLP-1 release.' Agreement on uncertainty about physiological utility.

Both evaluations address sensor sensitivity limitations (C66-C67). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inference about physiological levels and appropriate qualification of applications. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 'there may be biological situations where the concentration is adequate' but noting 'this is not established.' Partial disagreement on how well limitations are addressed.

Both evaluations support background/context claims (C1-C2, C9-C20, C68, C70). OpenEval notes these represent established knowledge from literature, appropriately cited. Peer review confirms these are 'established background facts cited from literature and are not disputed.' Complete agreement on contextual claims.

Both evaluations address DPPIV degradation limitation (C72-C73) but differ in assessment. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable speculation about brain applications though lacking experimental validation. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN and is 'more pessimistic about utility,' stating 'utility of PhotoGLP1 is therefore limited to acute (minutes) in vitro experiments.' Disagreement on severity of limitation.

OpenEval addresses sensor validation for screening (C6) supported by alanine scanning and clinical drug responses. Peer review R4 addresses ligand specificity (C35-C41) which overlaps with the pharmacological validation supporting C6. Both support the sensor's pharmacological validity for screening applications.

OpenEval addresses sensor utility for screening (C6) validated by alanine scanning data. Peer review R5 specifically addresses the alanine scanning validation (C42-C45), implicitly accepting this application. Both support the sensor's utility for structure-activity studies.

OpenEval R1 addresses sensor optimization including control variant C26. Peer review R2 specifically addresses C26, noting implicit acceptance as 'not specifically discussed by reviewers.' Both support the control variant as part of methodological validation.

Both evaluations address speculation about conformational selectivity (C65). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN within broader context of EC50 discrepancy, noting the interpretation is speculative. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, noting 'this speculation is not challenged by reviewers and follows logically from the accepted sensitivity measurements.' Disagreement on confidence level.

OpenEval R14 addresses photocaging context (C68, C70) as part of appropriate discussion comparing approaches. Peer review R15 groups these with other background claims as established facts not disputed. Both accept these contextual claims.

OpenEval R14 discusses photocaging advantages (C69) as appropriate context. Peer review R8 includes C69 in assessment of photo-GLP1 functionality, accepting the basic tool functionality. Both support the contextual framing of the photocaging approach.
